Within this framework, the causal-history dynamics generate a structural constraint compatible with γ_A. Within the two-channel integer-multiplicity family, (p,q)=(1,1) is further shown to be the unique discrete architecture compatible with the previously established DUT value γ_A, establishing algebraic uniqueness within this causal class. This consistency supports the interpretation of γ_A as a robust structural parameter of causal coarse-graining rather than a model-specific artifact. We develop a unified analysis based on the non-minimally coupled scalar action, exact compactification of z = ξS², slow–fast reduction, exact second-order response theory, minimal state-space realization, and Mori–Zwanzig projection. The exact transformation O = z/(1 + z), D = 1/(1 + z) implies D/O = 1/z. The microscopic response possesses a minimal two-dimensional realization and, away from critical damping, two distinct simple physical poles. Exact temporal sampling proves that the signed local scalar amplitude does not coincide with the positive history-counting variable, while projection onto the relevant scalar–curvature observable yields the explicit memory kernel K(t) = PLQ · e^(QLQt) · QLP; for the locally stationary damped realization this reduces to K(t) = −ω² · e^(−Γt), with effective projected resolvent G_eff(s) = (s + Γ)/(s² + Γs + ω²). The causal-history architecture is represented by two exhaustive, disjoint unit-cardinality extension classes, giving p = q = 1 and hence N_n = N_(n−1) + N_(n−2). The resulting ratio map R_(n+1) = 1/(1 + R_n) has the unique positive stable fixed point R_* = (√5 − 1)/2. Identifying the asymptotic ordered fraction with this scale-invariant ratio yields D/O = O and maps exactly to z_c = (1 + √5)/2. The resulting prediction γ_A = 0.618034 is fixed before observational comparison and is directly testable with Euclid, DESI, and CSST growth data.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202609.2210.v1\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 9, 24]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7197564\", \"title\": [\"Decoherence, Epistemic Coarse-Graining, and the Emergence of Classical Causal Structure\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>This paper demonstrates that classical causal structures necessarily emerge from the quantum formalism under the resource constraints of finite agents. Rather than interpreting decoherence as an objective physical collapse, this paper formalizes the partial trace operation as a minimal-entropy-increase completely positive and trace-preserving (CPTP) coarse-graining map, E = Tr ε , whose entropy increase ∆S and trace distance bound D ≤ O(e-t/τ D) quantify the epistemic horizon. The Kochen-Specker and Bell theorems falsify the existence of a global Kolmogorov joint probability and Reichenbach's Common Cause Principle at the pure quantum level, leaving Pearl's do-calculus undefined in the undecohered algebra A SE. By integrating the quantum Darwinism redundancy R δ ≫ 1 and the decoherent histories functional D(⃗ α, ⃗ β) = O(ε), this paper constructively proves that the approximate pointer algebra A p satisfies approximate Markovianity and modularity within an O(ε + δ) error bound, thereby establishing an effective do-operation that satisfies Pearl's truncated factorization formula. The causal asymmetry thus originates from the irreversibility of E rather than the time arrow of the Hamiltonian. Macroscopic causality is shown to be an effective topology necessarily adopted by finite agents to maintain Dutchbook consistency in empirical predictions.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7197564\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "2b46d6ae0369c422071ad14614237f6622e8756e4242d9d464d6eab465e32b97", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "causal_memory", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.1017/9781009024358.018", "doi:10.1103/physreve.85.041125", "doi:10.20944/preprints202609.2210.v1", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.7197564"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.1017/9781009024358.018", "https://doi.org/10.1103/physreve.85.041125", "https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202609.2210.v1", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7197564"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
